overhead_analysis.tradeoff_justification: ML-DSA-65 signatures are ~3.3 KB compared to 64 B for Ed25519. In HORA-Q, signatures are generated per-alert and per-evidence-vault entry rather than per raw packet wire-rate, making the 3.3 KB storage overhead easily negligible while providing unconditional post-quantum non-repudiation.

proposal_gap_closure_conclusion: Head-to-head empirical measurements confirm Enhanced HORA-Q achieves 0.0% baseline contamination compared to 66.7% for the naïve reference detector on attack vectors, while preserving 100% recall for malicious hijacks. Unlike the naïve detector, Enhanced HORA-Q distinguishes operational traffic engineering from malicious attacks by preserving uncertainty (MEDIUM confidence with explanatory reason) and quarantines unverified candidates. Post-quantum cryptographic overhead adds ~64.133 ms per alert signing, well within acceptable parameters for non-repudiable audit logging.
